item: Two figures tests no longer depend on what earlier files left in the shared test store
summary: WAL's shard 1 failed both slow-count tests in tests/test_figures_cold_start.py (avg_word_count None, then the failed state never reached) and its README said which earlier file was unknown. Measured: run in that shard's order (first 59 files), 32 articles, none with a word_count, sit in the one process-wide store when the file starts (the only files of that run that add articles are test_ai_custom_prompts, test_ai_keyword_evidence, test_country_wire, test_dateextract and test_evidence_review); the file's seed helper returned early on 'the table is not empty', so avg_word_count (an average over non-NULL counts) was None, and that failure left the slow count running behind the next test, which then never saw its failed state. One polluter test plus the old file reproduces both failures; the fixed file passes the same 59-file run (879 passed). The seed is now this file's own row keyed by URL with a word count, and the slow count is released in a finally. The twin, test_served_counts_cache.py::test_figures_are_served_stale_rather_than_recomputed_inline, failed alone on a clean main for the opposite reason (an empty store: _compute_figures_counted answers an empty corpus with the cheap figures only, so keyword_mentions_state never appears) and now seeds its own article. Test-only; no src change. Not claimed: that no other file depends on the shared store, which this does not audit.
